note: MADE-UP. Shaped on a real month of forecasting questions and trials; every store, person, figure and link is replaced.

ideas.label: Trial 0
ideas.title: Reproduce the shipped forecast
ideas.why: No trial result means anything until the shipped numbers reproduce.
ideas.tried: Nothing in the engine.
ideas.found: Pass (baseline).
ideas.status: Done.

ideas.label: Trial 1
ideas.title: Public holiday multiplier
ideas.why: 02-Oct-2026 (Gandhi Jayanti, a Friday) was the month's largest miss: Ridge 62.4% under (₹0.88 Cr), Meadow 22.5% under.
ideas.tried: - The public holiday is a fourth factor in the engine's day shape, beside weekday, day of month and festivals.
ideas.found: Pass on its own target, out of sample, in both regions.
ideas.status: Kept in the combined engine; code will be committed under a lab note.

ideas.label: Trial 2
ideas.title: Daily learning Run
ideas.why: A frozen forecast cannot see a change in the sales level until next month's Run.
ideas.tried: - Each day is forecast from the day before (a rolling origin) instead of once on 30-Sep-2026: 21 origins, 30-Sep-2026 to 20-Oct-2026, each reading actuals only up to its own origin.
ideas.found: Pass on its own targets; fails rule (a) as written, on bias, so the 06-Oct-2026 "accepted (provisional)" does not survive.
ideas.status: Kept in the combined engine, in the learning Run only; code will be committed under a lab note.

ideas.label: Trial 3
ideas.title: Festival-day guard on last year's day
ideas.why: 01-Oct-2025 to 03-Oct-2025 were autumn holiday days.
ideas.tried: A guard on "same date last year" (B1).
ideas.found: Fail. The direction is right: Ridge cell WAPE improves by 0.6 point.
ideas.status: Rejected.

ideas.label: Trial 3b
ideas.title: Drop last year's day on festival dates
ideas.why: Trial 3's placebo failed.
ideas.tried: The fallback for trial 3, aimed only at the festival dates themselves.
ideas.found: Fail. It lands the one cell it was built for, exactly, and otherwise does nothing for cell WAPE.
ideas.status: Rejected; not kept in the stack.

ideas.label: Trial 4
ideas.title: Festival_aligned weekly reset in Ridge
ideas.why: Trial 1 showed it cancels any day-level fix: with each week's total pinned to last year, the holiday lift can only move money between the days of the same week.
ideas.tried: festival_aligned is a Ridge adjustment applied after the engine.
ideas.found: Mixed. No option passes every test.
ideas.status: Open: festival-days-only result to be scored on the Harvest Festival.

ideas.label: Trial 5
ideas.title: Harvest Festival gets its own festival season
ideas.why: In the shipped fit, the autumn holiday's span reached into the Harvest Festival (peak 2.29x at T+15), and the Harvest Festival itself had no effect that passed the gate.
ideas.tried: A festival's span now stops at the midpoint to the nearest other festival within 60 days.
ideas.found: Waiting for data. The fit now does what the post-mortem asked, but the days it changes have not happened yet.
ideas.status: Waiting for the Harvest Festival scoring, 30-Oct-2026 to 08-Nov-2026.

ideas.label: Trial 6
ideas.title: Basis weights with minimum support and a 0.7 cap
ideas.why: As shipped, 3,033 of Ridge's 5,112 series put more than 0.7 on a single basis, carrying ₹30.57 Cr of October.
ideas.tried: A basis with fewer than 14 graded days gets no weight, and no basis takes more than 0.7 when two or more are supported.
ideas.found: Pass on its own targets; Ridge fails rule (a) on bias.
ideas.status: Kept only as the fallback; not used in the combined engine.

ideas.label: Trial 7
ideas.title: Separate weights for festival-window days
ideas.why: The engine fits one weight set per series for the month, so festival days and ordinary days share one blend.
ideas.tried: On top of trial 13, each series gets a second weight set for days within 7 days of a festival, fitted on those days only.
ideas.found: Fail (no gain).
ideas.status: Rejected.

ideas.label: Trial 7a
ideas.title: Basis weights per weekday
ideas.why: Data Lead asked for a day-wise forecast.
ideas.tried: On trial 2's day-ahead setup (month-total term off), each series gets one weight set per weekday instead of one for the whole month.
ideas.found: Fail (no gain), and it fails rule (a) on 6 Ridge and 5 Meadow days.
ideas.status: Rejected.

ideas.label: Trial 7b
ideas.title: Basis weights from their recent record
ideas.why: Data Lead asked for a day-wise forecast.
ideas.tried: On trial 2's day-ahead setup (month-total term off), for every target day each basis is scored on the series' last four same weekdays before the origin and weighted by its inverse error.
ideas.found: Fail (marginal).
ideas.status: Rejected; not kept.

ideas.label: Trial 8
ideas.title: Lift for festivals seen only once
ideas.why: Ridge data starts in April 2025, so every Ridge festival has been seen once; in Meadow, the autumn holiday and the Harvest Festival have.
ideas.tried: A festival seen only once cannot pass the engine's two-occurrence gate, so its lift is 1.0 and it is forecast as an ordinary day.
ideas.found: Pass in Ridge (kept in the combined engine).
ideas.status: Kept in the combined engine (Ridge, with the day-after fix); code will be committed under a lab note.

ideas.label: Trial 10
ideas.title: Current_price only on price-driven series
ideas.why: Post-mortem: Meadow Sugar is price-driven (September quantity -3% on last year, price +32%), and current_price fixed it.
ideas.tried: current_price (Meadow, Grocery) re-prices each series' forecast at its last 28 days' price per piece.
ideas.found: Fail. Sugar goes from 7% to 15% under.
ideas.status: Rejected; current_price stays as shipped.

ideas.label: Trial 11
ideas.title: Festival lift by weekday
ideas.why: Post-mortem: weekday and festival interact.
ideas.tried: The day shape multiplies weekday by festival lift as if the two were independent.
ideas.found: Fail (no gain).
ideas.status: Rejected; not in the combined engine.

ideas.label: Trial 12
ideas.title: Trend basis (a sixth basis)
ideas.why: Meadow's late-September drop left 01-Oct-2026 about 20% over-forecast.
ideas.tried: A sixth basis beside the five.
ideas.found: Fail. Cell WAPE improves by 0.5 point in Ridge and 0.8 in Meadow, but the totals get worse and the placebo fails.
ideas.status: Rejected.

ideas.label: Trial 13
ideas.title: Basis weights shrunk toward the subcategory's
ideas.why: As shipped, 3,033 of Ridge's 5,112 series put more than 0.7 on a single basis, carrying ₹30.57 Cr of October.
ideas.tried: Each series' own best weights are pulled toward the best weights of its subcategory across all stores, by n / (n + k), where n is the series' graded days.
ideas.found: Pass. It wins every held-out month in both regions and gives Meadow the largest October gain (1.2 points).
ideas.status: Kept in the combined engine; code will be committed under a lab note.

ideas.label: Trial 14
ideas.title: Growth split into price x quantity
ideas.why: Post-mortem: Meadow Sugar is price-driven (September quantity -3% on last year, price +32%), and current_price fixed it.
ideas.tried: This replaces current_price.
ideas.found: Fail. Sugar stays 22% under and Pomegranate goes 52% under.
ideas.status: Rejected; current_price stays as shipped.

ideas.label: Trial 15
ideas.title: 80% uncertainty band per cell
ideas.why: Cell WAPE is 30-50% at this grain.
ideas.tried: An 80% band around each cell's forecast; the forecast itself does not change.
ideas.found: Flag only. It covers 70-90% on ordinary days in both regions, and coverage drops on the days the forecast genuinely missed (Ridge's 19-Oct-2026 and 20-Oct-2026).
ideas.status: A flag only, not part of the forecast or the combined engine; a candidate for the daily watch.

ideas.label: Trial 17
ideas.title: Ignore new stores' test-bill days
ideas.why: Post-mortem cause 6.
ideas.tried: A store-day whose sales are below 1% of the store's median trading day is treated as a test bill, not trading.
ideas.found: Pass. It fixes a data defect, not a model choice: a test bill is not a trading day, and treating it as one cost 2.3 points of Ridge cell WAPE.
ideas.status: Kept in the combined engine; code will be committed under a lab note.

ideas.label: Trial 18
ideas.title: Small cells split by their recent share
ideas.why: The diagnostic found the error in the subcategory mix within a store's day, not in the totals.
ideas.tried: This runs on trial 2's day-ahead forecasts, locally, with no engine run.
ideas.found: Pass. It is the only trial that passes rule (a) as written.
ideas.status: Kept (pooled) in the combined engine, applied after the engine run; code will be committed under a lab note.

ideas.label: Trial 19
ideas.title: Learned model (LightGBM) over the five bases
ideas.why: A learned blend can weight the bases differently by festival distance, store or level, which fixed weights cannot.
ideas.tried: Instead of fixed weights, a LightGBM model learns a correction to an equal-weight blend of the bases.
ideas.found: Fail. Ridge got worse (35.0% to 36.6%), and it fails rule (a) on 19 Ridge and 8 Meadow days.
ideas.status: Rejected; not in the combined engine.

ideas.label: Trial combined
ideas.title: Trials 1, 2, 8 (Ridge), 13, 17 and 18 in one engine
ideas.why: Each trial was judged on its own setup, and their gains overlap.
ideas.tried: One engine with every change that worked, run day-ahead (21 origins, 30-Sep-2026 to 20-Oct-2026): trials 1, 2, 8 with its day-after fix (Ridge only), 13 and 17, then trial 18's small-cell split.
ideas.found: Pass. Better than trials 2 + 18 by 1.3 points in Ridge and 0.3 in Meadow.
ideas.status: Open: the best engine forecast so far, run read-only; nothing landed.

ideas.label: Model comparison
ideas.title: Forecast models: shared dataset and features for the new models
ideas.why: Models can only be compared if they see the same cleaned history and use only what was known the day before.
ideas.found: Kept. Every model in this epic reads it; the leak was removed before any comparison.
ideas.status: Code outside the repo in trials/sota/; data in trials/sota_data/.

ideas.label: Model comparison
ideas.title: Statistical baselines (ETS, Croston, TSB, seasonal naive)
ideas.why: Standard methods set the floor.
ideas.found: Rejected. None beats trials 2 + 18, and every boosting model in a lab note beats all of them.
ideas.status: Not used.

ideas.label: Model comparison
ideas.title: LightGBM day-ahead, with and without the engine's day shape
ideas.why: A global model learns each cell's level and momentum from all series at once.
ideas.found: Superseded. On its own it is beaten in both regions by XGBoost with Ridge and Meadow trained together (a lab note).
ideas.status: Code outside the repo in trials/sota/run_lgbm.py and run_lgbm2.py, which a lab note needs.

ideas.label: Model comparison
ideas.title: XGBoost and other gradient-boosting families
ideas.outcome: XGBoost (Ridge and Meadow together) best for Ridge
ideas.why: Ridge's data starts in April 2025, so none of its festivals has a previous year to align to.
ideas.found: Kept for Ridge: 3.9 points better than the combined engine on 01-Oct-2026 to 20-Oct-2026, and still ahead to 28-Oct-2026.
ideas.status: Code outside the repo in trials/sota/run_gbm.py, run with .venv-sota (it has xgboost; .venv does not).

ideas.label: Model comparison
ideas.title: LightGBM cells reconciled to Tweedie store-day totals
ideas.why: Absolute-error cells get the mix within a store's day right; Tweedie, aiming at the mean, gets the totals closer.
ideas.found: Kept for Meadow: 3.4 points better than the combined engine on 01-Oct-2026 to 20-Oct-2026.
ideas.status: Code outside the repo in trials/sota/reconcile.py and recon3.py.

ideas.label: Model comparison
ideas.title: Neural models (N-BEATSx, N-HiTS, TFT, TiDE, PatchTST, DeepAR, BiTCN)
ideas.why: Neural models learn shared patterns across thousands of series and take inputs known in advance, such as festival dates, directly.
ideas.found: Rejected as a forecast: none beats XGBoost, and most of Meadow's are worse than the engine.
ideas.status: Not used.

ideas.label: Model comparison
ideas.title: TimesFM foundation model, no training
ideas.outcome: sales-only kept as a blend candidate
ideas.why: It needs no training, and the inputs version might see a festival coming.
ideas.found: Kept as a blend candidate, sales only: as good as the leader on ordinary days.
ideas.status: Code outside the repo in trials/sota/ (run_tsfm*.py, merge_tsfm.py, probe_tsfm_days.py, and install_tsfm.sh for .venv-tsfm).

ideas.label: Model comparison
ideas.title: Direct month-ahead model for November
ideas.outcome: mixed, the third model for November
ideas.why: The models above need yesterday's sales; November is forecast once, from 28-Oct-2026, for 33 days.
ideas.found: Mixed. Close to the combined engine on the cells month-ahead, not better; it under-forecasts festival months.
ideas.status: Open: it feeds November.

ideas.label: Model comparison
ideas.title: Combining the three forecasts (closest of three, middle of three)
ideas.outcome: middle of three kept for month-ahead
ideas.why: Each model is closest on a different share of sales (Ridge: shipped 24%, combined 32%, new 44%), so a good rule could beat all three.
ideas.found: Mixed. The middle of three is kept month-ahead, as a column of the November forecast.
ideas.status: Open: it feeds November.

ideas.label: November check
ideas.title: Grocery by quantity or by value, and onion
ideas.outcome: only Meadow Grocery uses quantity x price, kept as is
ideas.why: A forecast of quantity x a fixed price misses a price rise.
ideas.found: Kept as is. Meadow Grocery keeps forecasting kg or pieces and multiplying them by the last 28 days' price.
ideas.status: Closed: nothing changes in the November forecast.

ideas.label: November check
ideas.title: Meadow toys and opticals weighted to the last 28 days
ideas.outcome: kept, to be switched on for the 31-Oct-2026 run
ideas.why: Models that learn from a year of history lag a range that has just expanded.
ideas.found: Kept. The override lowers the bias in both months and the store x month error over the two.
ideas.status: Closed: kept; built as layer (a) of the November runbook (trials/nov_1029/RUNBOOK_tomorrow.md), to be switched on for the 31-Oct-2026 run.

ideas.label: November check
ideas.title: Food court forecast from the food-court till, all 11 outlets
ideas.why: When this check started the retail forecast did not carry the the food-court till food court, and the share rules quoted for it gave different answers.
ideas.found: Kept, as its own section beside the retail forecast, never added into store totals: layer (b) of the November runbook.
ideas.status: Closed.

ideas.label: November check
ideas.title: the food-court till food court now inside Meadow store sales
ideas.outcome: about ₹0.54 Cr of Meadow's November, how it is shown still open
ideas.why: A separate the food-court till food court section (a lab note) beside a retail forecast that already holds the same sales would count them twice.
ideas.found: Data finding. The Meadow retail forecast already holds the the food-court till food court, so the the food-court till section must not be added on top of it.
ideas.status: Open: how November shows Meadow's food court is not settled.

ideas.label: November check
ideas.title: Store Kingsway's year-ago Harvest Festival replaced by the mature stores' lift
ideas.why: A store's opening weeks are not a guide to its next Harvest Festival.
ideas.found: Kept for shipped and combined.
ideas.status: Closed: kept; built as layer (f) of the November runbook, to be switched on for the 31-Oct-2026 run.

ideas.label: November check
ideas.title: Store Westbrook's bulk saree day excluded from Ridge's history
ideas.why: One order should not set the forecast for a whole region's weekend.
ideas.found: Excluded, before the Ridge models.
ideas.status: Closed: kept; built as step 3b of the November runbook, following trials/one_offs/RUNBOOK.md, to be switched on for the 31-Oct-2026 run.

ideas.label: November check
ideas.title: Gold sales data after the 30-Oct-2026 fix
ideas.why: On 29-Oct-2026 the gold table was not visible to the engine's identity, so this check was blocked.
ideas.found: Passed. The engine reads the same sales from gold as from marts.
ideas.status: Closed.

ideas.label: November check
ideas.title: November forecast rehearsal on sales to 29-Oct-2026
ideas.why: The 31-Oct-2026 run has to finish in one sitting, on checked code and data.
ideas.found: Passed. The pipeline runs end to end on checked data and pinned code.
ideas.status: Closed.

ideas.label: Business Head I1
ideas.title: Show model, uplift and final separately; spread the 6% uplift sensibly
ideas.why: The flat 6% adds about ₹1.32 Cr in Meadow and ₹2.85 Cr in Ridge. Model +3% plus 6% should give +9% over October, but the sheet showed +6.0%. A flat 6% does not suit price-driven lines like onion.
ideas.tried: Added base, uplift and final columns to every row; rechecked month totals against daily rates.
ideas.found: Meadow ₹24.65 Cr + ₹1.44 Cr = ₹26.09 Cr; Ridge ₹52.81 Cr + ₹3.17 Cr = ₹55.98 Cr. The +3% had been quoted per day (October has 31 days); on month totals the model is level with October. Food court exempted from the uplift.
ideas.status: In the 31-Oct revised file. Excluding price-driven lines is still to come. Goal: the model learns the ~4% November step so the uplift can go.
evidence: Email: Re: Nov 2026 Forecast and updates

ideas.label: Business Head I2
ideas.title: Check Harvest Festival timing in the Nov/Oct ratio (Ridge looked low at +1.2%)
ideas.why: Harvest Festival was 20-Oct-2025 and is 08-Nov-2026; Ridge forecast ₹55.93 Cr against October ₹55.25 Cr.
ideas.tried: Split Meadow ratios by Harvest Festival month; shifted Ridge last-year daily sales so Harvest Festival lands on 08-Nov.
ideas.found: Meadow shows ~4% Nov over Oct either way. Ridge range ₹49.88–55.5 Cr, so ₹55.98 Cr already sits just above it.
ideas.status: No change. Ridge has one year of history; watch the first week.
evidence: Email: Re: Nov 2026 Forecast and updates

ideas.label: Business Head I3
ideas.title: Lift Ridge fast-growing lines: toys and dry fruits
ideas.why: Westbrook toys about ₹4.30 L short and dry fruits about ₹5.59 L short of their recent run.
ideas.tried: Toys moved to the last-4-weeks method. Dry fruits analysed: growth is front-loaded and last Harvest Festival week was the season low.
ideas.found: Toys +₹5.76 L (Westbrook ₹12.81 L to ₹15.70 L), lifting Ridge to ₹55.98 Cr. Dry fruits not changed.
ideas.status: Toys kept on the 4-week method. Dry fruits rejected for now, open for discussion.
evidence: Email: Re: Nov 2026 Forecast and updates

ideas.label: Business Head I4
ideas.title: Meadow dry fruits mix: dates +77% against nuts +9%
ideas.why: Dates forecast growth looked out of line with nuts.
ideas.tried: Compared last year’s Harvest Festival and November for dates.
ideas.found: Dates sold strongly around Harvest Festival last year and dropped in November.
ideas.status: Rejected for now, still open.
evidence: Email: Re: Nov 2026 Forecast and updates

ideas.label: Business Head I5
ideas.title: Meadow Basic Veg under-forecast, Tropical Veg about ₹6.45 L high
ideas.why: Vegetable lines looked out of line with recent sales.
ideas.tried: Traced the gap to an item regrouping that shows only from Oct-26, and to price.
ideas.found: About ₹4.30 L of the Tropical gap is the regrouping; ₹1.98 L depends on price. Basic Veg would go from ₹22.70 L to ₹24.38 L with the usual November quantity rise.
ideas.status: Agreed in principle; comes with the vegetable price views.
evidence: Email: Re: Nov 2026 Forecast and updates

ideas.label: Business Head I6
ideas.title: Ridge kidswear lift too high (+108% against men +71%)
ideas.why: About ₹0.65 Cr at risk if kidswear does not lift that much.
ideas.tried: Nov-2023 not available (Ridge history starts Apr-2025); analysed last Harvest Festival’s run-up instead.
ideas.found: 65% of kids’ run-up fell in the final week against 57% for men. Shifted to 08-Nov: kids +93%, men +57%. Lined up on the Harvest Festival, kids running +1%, men −7%.
ideas.status: Forecast kept. Watch the first week.
evidence: Email: Re: Nov 2026 Forecast and updates

ideas.label: Business Head I7
ideas.title: Vegetable price scenarios, with kilos beside value
ideas.why: Onion moved ₹14.15 to ₹31.43/kg with quantity −34%. Onion scenarios run ₹19.78–33.5 L; onion, potato, garlic and tomato could move Meadow ±₹8.60–10.8 L.
ideas.tried: Confirmed the forecast carries the last 4 weeks’ price; corrected Tropical and Beans rows on like-for-like items.
ideas.found: Onion at ₹28.68 L, which is the ₹34.40/kg case. Tropical: price +59%, kilos −12%. Beans: +29%, −13%.
ideas.status: Accepted. A separate Meadow vegetables file is promised: kg and value, low/base/high price.
evidence: Email: Re: Nov 2026 Forecast and updates

ideas.label: Business Head I8
ideas.title: Food court aligned with the food-court till, store by store, shown separately
ideas.why: Lakeside food court about ₹2.58–3.0 L low; ₹7.93 L Meadow gap against the food-court till.
ideas.tried: Reconciled the gap line by line.
ideas.found: ₹6.63 L of lines have no SAP food-court code; the food-court till ₹2.30 L higher on the same items; the store till stores offset −₹1.00 L.
ideas.status: the food-court till forecast for its 11 outlets, the model for Greenfield, Riverside, Bayside and Stonereach. Food court shown separately at ₹0.68 Cr; Lakeside ₹29.57 L.
evidence: Email: Re: Nov 2026 Forecast and updates

ideas.label: Business Head I9
ideas.title: Lakeside store plan: ₹40.33 L below target, about 36% of the Meadow gap
ideas.why: Lakeside carries a large share of the Meadow gap to target.
ideas.tried: Broke the gap down by division and line.
ideas.found: Lakeside ₹8.13 Cr against ₹8.51 Cr target, a ₹37.93 L gap. Fashion ₹27.35 L, Home ₹8.51 L; Men Top ₹7.61 L, Fresh Fruit ₹5.12 L.
ideas.status: Forecast Lead offered to work on a plan.
evidence: Email: Re: Nov 2026 Forecast and updates

ideas.label: Business Head I10
ideas.title: Reporting hygiene: coverage split, reasons for zero-forecast rows, negative forecasts
ideas.why: Plan rows with zero forecast had no reason; some forecasts were negative; Pinecrest growth needed both bases.
ideas.tried: Added reasons, zeroed negatives, fixed labels and Pinecrest basis.
ideas.found: Reasons on 781 Meadow and 655 Ridge rows. Pinecrest +33.6% on both bases (the bulk sale was billed at 100% discount).
ideas.status: Done in the revised file.
evidence: Email: Re: Nov 2026 Forecast and updates

ideas.label: Business Head I11
ideas.title: Store-specific day-of-week index on a trailing 8 weeks, refreshed weekly
ideas.why: Meadow day-of-week index runs Sun 1.32 to Thu 0.83; weekend index by store ranges Willowmere 1.71 to Stonereach 1.25 and is stable year on year.
ideas.tried: Reproduced Business Head’s figures (13 of 15 within 0.01). Tested 8, 13 and 26 weeks, a blend and a decaying average.
ideas.found: None passed in Meadow or Ridge; 8 weeks was the weakest. The model already has a pattern per store × subcategory.
ideas.status: Current weekday pattern kept.
evidence: Email: Re: Nov 2026 Forecast and updates (01-Nov pattern notes)

ideas.label: Business Head I12
ideas.title: Month-phase factor: Grocery salary week
ideas.why: Grocery days 1–7 run at 1.08–1.17×.
ideas.tried: Checked all 70 months of history against the model’s day-of-month curve.
ideas.found: Grocery is above average in days 1–7 in all 70 months (~1.15×); the model already carries it within 0.02.
ideas.status: No change. Month-end smoothing of the Grocery curve to be tested.
evidence: Email: Re: Nov 2026 Forecast and updates (01-Nov pattern notes)

ideas.label: Business Head I13
ideas.title: Treat holiday weekdays as Saturday, plus a Harvest Festival override
ideas.why: Holidays on weekdays trade like weekends.
ideas.tried: Tested on every weekday holiday since 2025.
ideas.found: Improved accuracy and bias on only 2 of 9 holidays. Meadow Harvest Festival lifts vary by year.
ideas.status: No override. Watch 3–5 Nov; autumn holiday days in the holiday list to be tested.
evidence: Email: Re: Nov 2026 Forecast and updates (01-Nov pattern notes)

ideas.label: Business Head I14
ideas.title: Phase daily targets on a 364-day weekday-aligned last year
ideas.why: Weekday alignment should make daily targets fairer.
ideas.tried: Compared with the warehouse’s rule (last year’s same-weekday average).
ideas.found: Current rule beat a 364-day shift in 5 of 5 checks. Weak spot: the Harvest Festival window; in October that rule did worse (Meadow 17% against 12% error).
ideas.status: Business Head to choose: test a corrected festival-window phasing, or load the forecast as November’s target.
evidence: Email: Re: Nov 2026 Forecast and updates (01-Nov pattern notes)

ideas.label: Business Head I15
ideas.title: Do not judge stores on daily contribution %
ideas.why: A store’s share of the day swings with the weekday.
ideas.tried: Discussed.
ideas.found: Agreed.
ideas.status: Stores judged against their own weekday-adjusted target.
evidence: Email: Re: Nov 2026 Forecast and updates (01-Nov pattern notes)

ideas.label: Business Head I16
ideas.title: Store hourly profiles (bus-town vs evening stores) for staffing
ideas.why: Eastfield, Hillview, Bayside and Riverside peak at noon with 16–22% of bills after 7 pm; Willowmere does 34.4%.
ideas.tried: Reproduced within 0.1; checked value, weekends and month-to-month stability; clustered stores.
ideas.found: Pattern holds. Lakeside sits with the daytime group, so it is more a gradient. All 7 Ridge stores are evening stores.
ideas.status: The forecast is daily only. Staffing needs till throughput and shift rules from operations.
ideas.revisit: When hourly forecasting is in scope
evidence: Email: Re: Nov 2026 Forecast and updates (01-Nov pattern notes)

questions.q: Show the model, the 6% uplift and the final separately, and spread the uplift sensibly
questions.ask: The 6% adds about ₹1.32 Cr in Meadow and ₹2.85 Cr in Ridge. Model +3% plus 6% should give about +9% over October, but the sheet shows +6.0%. A flat 6% does not suit price-driven lines like onion.
questions.ans: Base, uplift and final are now on every row. Meadow ₹24.65 Cr + ₹1.44 Cr = ₹26.09 Cr; Ridge ₹52.81 Cr + ₹3.17 Cr = ₹55.98 Cr. The +3% had been quoted per day (October has 31 days); on month totals the model is level with October. Food court is now exempt from the uplift.
questions.follow: Excluding price-driven lines from the uplift: next revision

questions.q: Is Ridge's November too low once Harvest Festival timing is allowed for?
questions.ask: Harvest Festival was 20-Oct-2025 and is 08-Nov-2026, yet Ridge's November (₹55.93 Cr) is only +1.2% on October (₹55.25 Cr).
questions.ans: Split Meadow's ratios by Harvest Festival month: about +4% either way. Shifted Ridge's last-year days so Harvest Festival falls on 08-Nov: range ₹49.88–55.5 Cr, so ₹55.98 Cr already sits just above it.
questions.follow: Watch the first week of November

questions.q: Ridge toys and dry fruits look short of their recent run
questions.ask: Westbrook toys about ₹4.30 L short and dry fruits about ₹5.59 L short.
questions.ans: Toys moved to the last-4-weeks method: +₹5.76 L (Westbrook ₹12.81 L to ₹15.70 L). Dry fruits not changed: growth is front-loaded and last Harvest Festival week was the season low.

questions.q: Why do dates grow +77% when nuts grow +9%?
questions.ask: The dry fruits mix looks out of line.
questions.ans: Dates sold strongly around Harvest Festival last year and dropped in November; the forecast follows that.

questions.q: Basic Veg looks under-forecast and Tropical Veg about ₹6.45 L high
questions.ask: Both lines look out of line with recent sales.
questions.ans: About ₹4.30 L of the Tropical gap is an item regrouping that shows only from Oct-26; ₹1.98 L depends on price. Basic Veg would go from ₹22.70 L to ₹24.38 L with the usual November quantity rise.
questions.impact: Basic Veg ₹22.70 L → ₹24.38 L if adopted
questions.follow: Comes with the vegetable price file

questions.q: Kidswear lift (+108%) looks too high against men (+71%)
questions.ask: About ₹0.65 Cr at risk if kidswear does not lift that much.
questions.ans: Nov-2023 is not available (Ridge history starts Apr-2025). Last Harvest Festival: 65% of the kids' run-up fell in the final week, against 57% for men. Lined up on the Harvest Festival, kids are running +1% and men −7%.
questions.follow: Watch the first week of November

questions.q: Give vegetable price scenarios, with kilos beside value
questions.ask: Onion moved ₹14.15 to ₹31.43/kg with quantity −34%. Onion alone runs ₹19.78–33.5 L across scenarios; onion, potato, garlic and tomato could move Meadow ±₹8.60–10.8 L.
questions.ans: The forecast carries the last 4 weeks' price (onion ₹28.68 L, the ₹34.40/kg case). Tropical and Beans corrected on like-for-like items. A separate Meadow vegetables file is promised: kg and value, low/base/high price.

questions.q: Align food court with the food-court till, store by store, and show it separately
questions.ask: Lakeside food court about ₹2.58–3.0 L low; Meadow ₹7.93 L below the food-court till.
questions.ans: Gap explained: ₹6.63 L of lines have no SAP food-court code; the food-court till ₹2.30 L higher on the same items; the the store till stores offset −₹1.00 L. the food-court till's forecast now used for its 11 outlets, the model for Greenfield, Riverside, Bayside and Stonereach.
questions.impact: Food court shown separately, ₹0.68 Cr; Lakeside ₹29.57 L

questions.q: What is the plan for Lakeside's gap to target?
questions.ask: Lakeside is ₹40.33 L below target, about 36% of the Meadow gap.
questions.ans: Lakeside ₹8.13 Cr against ₹8.51 Cr target, a ₹37.93 L gap. Fashion ₹27.35 L, Home ₹8.51 L; Men Top ₹7.61 L, Fresh Fruit ₹5.12 L. Offered to work on a plan.

questions.q: Coverage split, reasons for zero-forecast rows, negative forecasts, Pinecrest on both bases
questions.ask: Plan rows with a zero forecast had no reason; some forecasts were negative.
questions.ans: Reasons added to 781 Meadow and 655 Ridge rows; negative forecasts set to zero; labels fixed. Pinecrest is +38.1% on both bases (the bulk sale was billed at 100% discount).

questions.q: Use a store-specific weekday index on a trailing 8 weeks, refreshed weekly
questions.ask: Meadow's weekday index runs Sun 1.32 to Thu 0.83; the weekend index ranges Willowmere 1.71 to Stonereach 1.25 and is stable year on year.
questions.ans: Reproduced (13 of 15 within 0.01). Tested 8, 13 and 26 weeks, a blend and a decaying average: none passed in Meadow or Ridge, and 8 weeks was the weakest. The model already has a weekday pattern per store × subcategory.

questions.q: Add a salary-week factor for Grocery
questions.ans: Grocery is above average in days 1–7 in all 70 months (about 1.15×); the model already carries that day-of-month curve, within 0.02.
questions.follow: Test month-end smoothing of the Grocery curve

questions.q: Treat holiday weekdays as Saturdays, and override Harvest Festival
questions.ask: Holidays on weekdays trade like weekends.
questions.ans: Improved accuracy on only 2 of 9 weekday holidays since 2025; Meadow's Harvest Festival lift varies by year. No override.
questions.follow: Watch 03–05 Nov; test the autumn holiday days

questions.q: Phase daily targets on a 364-day, weekday-aligned last year
questions.ask: Weekday alignment should make daily targets fairer.
questions.ans: The current rule (last year's same-weekday average) beat a 364-day shift in 5 of 5 checks. Weak spot: the Harvest Festival window, where October's error was 17% against 12%. Choice for Business Head: test a corrected festival-window phasing, or load the forecast as November's target.

questions.q: Do not judge stores on daily contribution %
questions.ask: A store's share of the day swings with the weekday.
questions.ans: Agreed. Stores are judged against their own weekday-adjusted target.

questions.q: Use store hourly profiles (bus-town vs evening) for hourly sales and staffing
questions.ask: Eastfield, Hillview, Bayside and Riverside peak at noon with 16–22% of bills after 7 pm; Willowmere does 34.4%.
questions.ans: Reproduced within 0.1; the pattern holds on value and at weekends. Lakeside sits with the daytime group. All 7 Ridge stores are evening stores. The forecast is daily only; staffing needs till throughput and shift rules from operations.
questions.follow: When hourly forecasting is in scope
